scope: Illustrate the GPT-1 Extract readout in both existing editions and continue the same NLI example at the GPT-2 vocabulary-output subsection.

review.sources: Radford et al. §§3.1–3.3 and 4.1–4.2, Figure 1; Stanford CS224N Winter 2023 lecture 9, slides 40–46, and archived course reuse notice under Logistics; pinned OpenAI train.py for Extract pooling in the released Story Cloze experiment.
review.workedCase: The nine-position NLI example pools h8 above Extract. Causal masking would prevent a first-position Extract from reading the two sentences. The 768-by-3 class matrix gives one logit per relation, unlike GPT-2's vocabulary head at Relation:, where a two-token label requires two conditional probabilities. Keep the numerical worked example and the distinction between the paper's NLI recipe and the released Story Cloze implementation.
review.style: Read both complete chapter inputs before editing. Keep two-stage examples, equations, results and citations; replace the repeated conclusion with the concrete transition. Distinguish the main supervised protocol from GPT-1's zero-shot experiments.
review.provenance: Manning's original slide-41 diagram, including arrows, both rows and all labels; from the archived lecture PDF at 240 dpi. Stanford's course page permits use and requests acknowledgment. No permission for the separate OpenAI paper artwork is inferred; its panels remain linked only.
review.verification: 2083 pages built; 30 focused and 320 built-output tests passed; zero broken internal links. Both standalone GPT-1 examples and the original Story Cloze serialization checks ran on CPU. Chrome at 1280 and 375 CSS px in both languages confirmed the exact image hash, column fit, zoom, source caption and a working link to the same-locale GPT-2 example. Visually inspected the inline diagram at desktop and mobile widths.

## Наследие и переход к GPT-2

GPT-1 объединяет причинное языковое предобучение и перенос всех параметров
на разные размеченные задачи. Форматы входа позволяют сохранить один
Transformer, а головы определяют, какой ответ нужен: метка, оценка
близости или индекс кандидата.

В [[02 Areas/ML & DL/00 Учебник/06 Encoder, Decoder и Encoder-Decoder/05 GPT-2 — zero-shot через язык|GPT-2]]
авторы увеличат модель и корпус и будут исследовать выполнение задач
через текстовый префикс без отдельного supervised fine-tuning. Такой
интерфейс нужно отличать от описанных здесь обучаемых голов GPT-1.

## Источники и дальнейшее чтение
changes.new:
## Наследие и переход к GPT-2

В нашем примере GPT-1 выбирает класс из трёх логитов над `Extract`.
В [[00 Учебник/06 Encoder, Decoder и Encoder-Decoder/05 GPT-2 — zero-shot через язык#gpt2-relation-prefix|том же примере с GPT-2]]
последняя позиция запроса — двоеточие в `Relation:`. Словарная
голова оценивает следующий токен. Если метка занимает два токена,
одного выхода на двоеточии не хватит: вероятность второго токена
зависит от первого. Такой способ выбора уже встречался в zero-shot
опытах GPT-1; в статье о GPT-2 авторы проверяют его и другие способы
задать задачу через текст без отдельного дообучения.

changes.old:
## Legacy and the transition to GPT-2

GPT-1 combines causal language pre-training with transfer of all parameters
to different labeled tasks. Input formats retain one Transformer, while
heads specify the required answer: a label, similarity score, or candidate index.

In [[02 Areas/ML & DL/00 Учебник/06 Encoder, Decoder и Encoder-Decoder/05 GPT-2 — zero-shot через язык|GPT-2]],
the authors enlarge model and corpus and investigate task execution
through a text prefix without separate supervised fine-tuning.
That interface differs from GPT-1's trained heads described here.

## Sources and further reading
changes.new:
## Legacy and the transition to GPT-2

In our example, GPT-1 chooses a class from three logits above `Extract`.
In [[00 Учебник/06 Encoder, Decoder и Encoder-Decoder/05 GPT-2 — zero-shot через язык#gpt2-relation-prefix|the same example with GPT-2]],
the final position is the colon in `Relation:`. The vocabulary head
scores the next token. If a label takes two tokens, the output at the
colon is not enough: the second token's probability depends on the
first. GPT-1 already used this kind of scoring in its zero-shot tests.
The GPT-2 paper studies this and other ways to express a task in text
without separate fine-tuning.
